summary.headline: Rubicon Q1 FY27 revenue rose 52% YoY to INR5,343 million and operating EBITDA margin hit 24.2%; FY27 EBITDA margin guide raised to 23%.
summary.overview:
Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR5,343 million, up 52% YoY, with operating EBITDA of INR1,291 million (24.2% margin) and PAT of INR848 million including a one-off insurance claim in other income. Gross margin rose about 140 bps QoQ to 67.7% as management gave up lower-margin US business and reduced reliance on contract manufacturing. USD revenue was USD55 million, up 32% YoY but slightly down QoQ. Operating cash flow was weak at INR285 million due to delayed GST refunds, which management expects to normalise in Q2. Arinna Lifesciences (acquired April 2026) contributed about INR12 crore of revenue and immaterial EBITDA. Management also announced a CFO transition and the acquisition of a New Jersey manufacturing site.</overview>

segments.name: India business
segments.commentary: Indian revenue grew 9.7% YoY, per analyst question on the India vs US split; management did not dispute the figure.

segments.name: US business
segments.commentary: US revenue grew about 4% YoY per analyst figure, as management walked away from lower-margin US business; specialty share of gross profit rose.

segments.name: Arinna Lifesciences
segments.commentary: Acquired April 2026; contributed about INR12 crore revenue in Q1 with immaterial EBITDA. Management is in a growth-fixing phase this year before focusing on profitability.

guidance_outlook: FY27 operating EBITDA margin guidance raised to around 23% from the earlier 22-23% range, despite ESOP, Arinna growth and pre-revenue facility costs.
Working capital guided at 125-130 days, per earlier guidance.
Q2 FY27 USD revenue tracking strongly sequentially; cash flow expected to be healthy in Q2 as GST refunds normalise.
Pithampur facility to ramp up commercial operations from Q1 CY2027.
New Jersey (East Brunswick) site expected to start commercialisation in CY2027 after quality management system implementation.
R&D spend target of INR500 crore over nine quarters (FY26, FY27 and Q1 FY28); INR251 crore spent so far at about INR60 crore per quarter. R&D to remain 10-11% of revenue.
capex_capacity: Pithampur site is about 30 acres, of which only 5-6 acres are in use; management says capacity can be scaled gradually over the next 9-12 months and expanded further over 2-3 years.
Pithampur FDA inspection in early July 2026 produced a 483 with two procedural observations; management says these were responded to and FDA approval on a regulatory filing followed.
New Jersey (East Brunswick) site acquired via court-supervised bankruptcy for USD2.9 million; FDA inspection in May 2026 resulted in VAI status; site is adjacent to AIMRX 3PL distribution operations.
CSN facility is modularly ready for niche dosage forms.
Management said capex will always lag sales and capacity is being added based on revenue visibility; outsourcing remains part of the mix.
demand_pricing: Top 5 products were 39% of revenue and top 10 were 55% in Q1; concentration broadly stable over last four quarters.
Management said pricing remains stable, supported by specialty and differentiated portfolio.
Gross margin pressure in prior quarters came from higher outsourced manufacturing; tactical exits from lower-margin US business were made.
Management claims R&D productivity of about 5.5x on annualised Q1 FY27 revenue, versus 3.3x on the earlier cohort (INR165 crore R&D vs about INR540 crore incremental revenue).
Management said it ranks number one across the six IPO-showcased products; market shares are broadly stable to up.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked whether approvals are slowing and how to think about the pipeline and specialty churn.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said approvals are on the planned trajectory and it is not slowing; it declined to give a specialty product count or churn beyond annual disclosure.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked how the New Jersey site changes the US/India manufacturing footprint and margins.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the site is strategic (government/VA business, onshore supply, risk diversification) and expects it to be margin accretive, without quantifying.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst queried the link between cost of materials, purchases and a large revenue increase, and transfer pricing.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said transfer pricing is compliant with no sharp movement, attributed the mix to own manufacturing, outsourcing and traded goods, and offered to take the query offline.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked how Arinna margins will evolve.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Arinna is in phases: growth identification this year, then beating IPM growth, then profitability; the FY27 EBITDA guidance includes Arinna growth investment.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the capacity headroom at Pithampur.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 30 acres at Pithampur with only 5-6 acres used, with capacity to be scaled over 9-12 months and expanded further over 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked why the FDA-under-review count (24 ANDAs/NDAs given last year) was not updated.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the count is disclosed once a year and was shared in the Q4 call.

risks_watch: Operating cash flow of INR285 million; management expects the GST refund delay to normalise in Q2, so watch Q2 cash conversion.
Gross margin dependent on the own-vs-outsourced manufacturing mix; Pithampur and New Jersey ramp timing (CY2027) is key.
Pre-revenue costs (Pithampur, New Jersey, Arinna growth spend and ESOP) will weigh on EBITDA through FY27.
US tariff exposure: an analyst noted about 97% of exports go to the US; management did not address tariff mitigation directly.
Limited disclosure on pipeline, specialty product count and product-level approvals; management says the 24-product FDA count will be given annually.
Analyst queries on transfer pricing and inventory movement were not resolved on the call; management offered an offline follow-up.
